# PRD -- Slice 10: Automation-Policy / Tier-Band Configuration

Sprint: Phase 3 / Workstream Platform
Status: Proposed (2026-07-19)
Ticket handle: PAXOS-S10-TIERPOLICY
Owner: Platform Engineering
Last updated: 2026-07-19

================================================================================
1. PROBLEM SUMMARY
================================================================================

The tier router (agents/nodes/tier_router.py) is today a fully hard-coded
deterministic function: confidence bands (>=0.95 -> routine, 0.70-0.94 ->
complex, <0.70 -> exception) and the exception-escalation signals (generic
resolution, drug-alias, counter-offer, novel denial reason) are compile-time
constants. This was the right choice to satisfy Illinois and Maryland HB 1563
("never an LLM deciding tier") and to ship fast, but it creates a growing
operational problem:

1. Different clients operate under different regulatory regimes. A payer in
   California has different HITL thresholds than one in Illinois. The Illinois
   0.95 floor is a statutory floor, not a universal one. There is no per-tenant
   or per-drug-class configuration.

2. The hard-coded constants are not observable. There is no API to inspect what
   tier bands are active for a given tenant or to see the history of tier
   changes.

3. Compliance teams cannot tune bands without a code deploy. A client needing
   a stricter routine threshold (e.g., >=0.98) has no recourse.

4. Promotions from exception to complex tier after human validation are not
   tracked. Once a drug/plan pair has been successfully processed as exception
   N times and always approved, the platform cannot surface that signal to help
   an admin propose a band adjustment.

5. The TierBand concept in doc 10 ("Automation-Policy / Tier-Band
   Configuration") is a named roadmap item with no implementation and no data
   model.

================================================================================
2. GOALS
================================================================================

1. Introduce a TierPolicy domain object that encodes the confidence bands,
   escalation signals, and optional per-tenant/per-drug-class overrides,
   persisted in PostgreSQL.

2. Expose a GET /api/admin/tier-policy and PATCH /api/admin/tier-policy
   management surface (platform-admin or tenant-admin role only).

3. Refactor tier_router.py to load the active TierPolicy at request time (from
   a cached policy store) rather than compile-time constants, while keeping the
   function deterministic and LLM-free (the statutory requirement is
   unchanged).

4. Emit a tier_policy_snapshot field on AuditRecord recording which policy
   version governed each routing decision -- a regulatory compliance artifact.

5. Add a TierBandHistory table tracking every policy change (who, when, old
   value, new value) for audit trail completeness.

6. Implement a band-promotion signal aggregator: a background read-only query
   over audit_records that surfaces drug/plan pairs where exception-tier runs
   consistently resulted in human approval, for an admin to use as evidence
   when proposing a band adjustment.

7. Add a GET /api/admin/tier-policy/promotion-signals endpoint returning these
   signals (read-only; no automatic band changes -- the human remains in the
   loop per the statutory requirement).

8. Produce complete test coverage: unit tests for policy loading and routing
   under overrides; integration tests for the management endpoints; contract
   tests for parity between the new policy models and src/types.ts.

================================================================================
3. NON-GOALS
================================================================================

- Automatic tier-band adjustment without human approval. The promotion-signal
  aggregator is a read-only advisory surface; it never modifies the active
  policy autonomously. Any band change requires an explicit PATCH call by an
  authorized user.

- LLM-based tier decisions. The statutory requirement (Illinois, MD HB 1563)
  is unchanged: tier routing is deterministic, never LLM-decided. This slice
  makes the constants configurable, not the routing logic.

- Per-case tier override by a reviewer. An individual reviewer cannot override
  a tier decision post-hoc through this slice. That is a separate
  exception-resolution surface (related to break-glass / O13).

- Real-time policy push. Policy changes take effect on the next request; there
  is no live-push or mid-stream policy change.

- UI policy editor. The Build-view policy editor in the demo is fixture-driven.
  Wiring it to the live endpoints is a Workstream SU task (capability manifest
  unit B8).

================================================================================
4. REQUIREMENTS
================================================================================

Functional
----------

P-1  TierPolicy model: policy_id (UUID), tenant_id (FK, nullable -- null =
     platform default), version (int, monotonic), routine_floor (float, 0-1,
     default 0.95), complex_floor (float, 0-1, default 0.70),
     exception_signals (list of ExceptionSignal enum values),
     drug_class_overrides (list of DrugClassBand), effective_from (datetime),
     created_by (user_id), is_active (bool).

P-2  DrugClassBand model: drug_class (str), routine_floor (float),
     complex_floor (float). Per-drug-class overrides take precedence over the
     tenant-level policy; the most specific match wins.

P-3  ExceptionSignal enum: generic_resolution, drug_alias_first_pairing,
     counter_offer, novel_denial_reason, gatekeeper_exhausted. Mirrors the
     existing hard-coded escalation logic; the policy controls which signals
     are active.

P-4  tier_router.py loads the active TierPolicy for the current tenant_id at
     request time via PolicyStore.get_active(tenant_id) -> TierPolicy. Policy
     is cached (TTL 60 s) to avoid a DB round-trip per request; a stale cache
     is safe (a policy change takes effect within the TTL window).

P-5  decide_tier(signals: TierSignals, policy: TierPolicy) -> CaseTier
     replaces the current decide_tier(signals: TierSignals) -> CaseTier
     signature. The existing band logic is identical but parameterized over
     policy.routine_floor, policy.complex_floor, and
     policy.exception_signals.

P-6  AuditRecord gains tier_policy_id: str and tier_policy_version: int,
     written at the same boundary as the rest of the record (before the
     terminal SSE event).

P-7  GET /api/admin/tier-policy returns the active policy for the caller's
     tenant (or the platform default for platform-admin/Bearer).

P-8  PATCH /api/admin/tier-policy accepts a TierPolicyUpdate body and creates
     a new policy version (immutable history; the old version is deactivated,
     not mutated). Only tenant_admin or platform_admin role may call this
     endpoint.

P-9  Every PATCH writes a TierBandHistory row: history_id, tenant_id,
     changed_by (user_id), changed_at, old_policy_id, new_policy_id,
     diff_summary (JSONB of changed fields).

P-10 GET /api/admin/tier-policy/history returns TierBandHistory rows for the
     caller's tenant, newest first (platform-admin/Bearer sees all tenants).

P-11 GET /api/admin/tier-policy/promotion-signals queries audit_records for
     drug/plan pairs where:
       (a) tier was exception
       (b) provenance became human_edited (approved by a reviewer)
       (c) this has happened >= N times (configurable threshold, default 5)
     Returns a PromotionSignal list: drug, plan_id, exception_count,
     human_approved_count, suggested_complex_floor (a conservative estimate,
     never applied automatically).

P-12 The platform default TierPolicy is seeded at Alembic migration time with
     the Illinois statutory values (routine_floor=0.95, complex_floor=0.70,
     all exception signals active). It can only be changed by a platform_admin
     caller.

Non-functional
--------------

P-13 Policy cache is per-worker; a cache miss results in at most one DB read
     per TTL window per tenant per worker.

P-14 decide_tier remains a pure function (no I/O); policy is loaded by the
     node wrapper, not inside the pure function.

P-15 tier_policy_id + tier_policy_version in AuditRecord must be present for
     every post-S10 run; pre-S10 records have nullable fields (additive
     column, existing rows unaffected).

P-16 All PATCH /api/admin/tier-policy calls are logged as AuditRecord rows
     with lifecycle=policy_change, so the audit trail captures both case
     events and configuration changes in one table.

P-17 routine_floor must be >= complex_floor + 0.01; the API returns 422 if
     violated.

P-18 promotion-signals query is read-only and bounded: the aggregation runs
     over at most the last 90 days of records (configurable via
     PROMOTION_LOOKBACK_DAYS env var).

================================================================================
5. WORKFLOW MODELING
================================================================================

Policy resolution at routing time
-----------------------------------

  run_tier_router(state: PipelineState) -> PipelineState
          |
          v
  policy = PolicyStore.get_active(state.request.tenant_id)
          |  (cache hit: no DB;
          |   cache miss: SELECT FROM tier_policies
          |               WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND is_active = true;
          |               fallback to platform default if none found)
          |
          v
  tier_signals = TierSignals.from_state(state)
          |
          v
  tier = decide_tier(tier_signals, policy)    <- pure, parameterized
          |
          v
  state["tier"]                = tier
  state["tier_policy_id"]      = policy.policy_id
  state["tier_policy_version"] = policy.version
          |
          v
  return state

Policy update flow
-------------------

  PATCH /api/admin/tier-policy
          |
          v
  auth_middleware -> role must be tenant_admin or platform_admin (403 otherwise)
          |
          v
  validate TierPolicyUpdate
  (routine_floor >= complex_floor + 0.01 -- 422 if not)
          |
          v
  BEGIN TRANSACTION
    INSERT INTO tier_policies (..., version = old_version + 1, is_active = true)
    UPDATE tier_policies SET is_active = false
      WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND policy_id != new_id
    INSERT INTO tier_band_history
      (old_policy_id, new_policy_id, diff_summary, ...)
  COMMIT
          |
          v
  PolicyStore.invalidate_cache(tenant_id)
          |
          v
  AuditRecord(lifecycle=policy_change, correlation_id=new_policy_id, ...)
          |
          v
  200 { active_policy: TierPolicy }

Promotion-signal aggregation (read-only)
-----------------------------------------

  GET /api/admin/tier-policy/promotion-signals
          |
          v
  auth_middleware -> tenant_admin or platform_admin (403 otherwise)
          |
          v
  SELECT drug, plan_id,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE tier = 'exception') AS exception_count,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE tier = 'exception'
                          AND provenance = 'human_edited') AS approved_count
  FROM audit_records
  WHERE tenant_id = $1
    AND created_at >= now() - INTERVAL '$PROMOTION_LOOKBACK_DAYS days'
  GROUP BY drug, plan_id
  HAVING approved_count >= $PROMOTION_THRESHOLD
          |
          v
  suggested_complex_floor =
    approved_count / exception_count * active_policy.complex_floor
    (conservative -- never exceeds active_policy.routine_floor - 0.01)
          |
          v
  PromotionSignalsResponse { signals, generated_at, policy_id, lookback_days }

================================================================================
6. DATA MODEL CHANGES
================================================================================

New database tables (alembic/versions/0002_tier_policy.py)
-----------------------------------------------------------

  CREATE TABLE tier_policies (
      policy_id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      tenant_id            UUID REFERENCES tenants(tenant_id),  -- NULL = platform default
      version              INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
      routine_floor        FLOAT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.95,
      complex_floor        FLOAT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.70,
      exception_signals    JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT
                             '["generic_resolution","drug_alias_first_pairing",
                               "counter_offer","novel_denial_reason",
                               "gatekeeper_exhausted"]'::jsonb,
      drug_class_overrides JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
      effective_from       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      created_by           UUID REFERENCES users(user_id),
      is_active            BOOL NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
      UNIQUE (tenant_id, version)
  );
  CREATE INDEX tier_policy_active_idx ON tier_policies(tenant_id, is_active);

  CREATE TABLE tier_band_history (
      history_id    UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      tenant_id     UUID,
      changed_by    UUID REFERENCES users(user_id),
      changed_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      old_policy_id UUID REFERENCES tier_policies(policy_id),
      new_policy_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tier_policies(policy_id),
      diff_summary  JSONB NOT NULL
  );

audit_records additions (additive, nullable for pre-S10 rows):

  ALTER TABLE audit_records ADD COLUMN tier_policy_id      UUID;
  ALTER TABLE audit_records ADD COLUMN tier_policy_version INT;

New Python models (backend/models/schemas.py)
----------------------------------------------

  class ExceptionSignal(str, Enum):
      generic_resolution       = "generic_resolution"
      drug_alias_first_pairing = "drug_alias_first_pairing"
      counter_offer            = "counter_offer"
      novel_denial_reason      = "novel_denial_reason"
      gatekeeper_exhausted     = "gatekeeper_exhausted"

  class DrugClassBand(BaseModel):
      drug_class    : str    # e.g., "GLP-1", "immunosuppressant"
      routine_floor : float  # 0.0-1.0
      complex_floor : float  # 0.0-1.0; must be < routine_floor - 0.01

  class TierPolicy(BaseModel):
      policy_id            : str
      tenant_id            : str | None   # None = platform default
      version              : int
      routine_floor        : float = 0.95
      complex_floor        : float = 0.70
      exception_signals    : list[ExceptionSignal]
      drug_class_overrides : list[DrugClassBand] = []
      effective_from       : datetime
      created_by           : str | None
      is_active            : bool

  class TierPolicyUpdate(BaseModel):
      model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True)
      routine_floor        : float | None = None
      complex_floor        : float | None = None
      exception_signals    : list[ExceptionSignal] | None = None
      drug_class_overrides : list[DrugClassBand] | None = None
      rationale            : str    # <= 1000 chars -- required for audit trail

  class TierBandHistoryEntry(BaseModel):
      history_id    : str
      tenant_id     : str | None
      changed_by    : str | None
      changed_at    : datetime
      old_policy_id : str | None
      new_policy_id : str
      diff_summary  : dict

  class PromotionSignal(BaseModel):
      drug                  : str
      plan_id               : str
      exception_count       : int
      human_approved_count  : int
      suggested_complex_floor : float   # advisory only; never applied automatically

  class PromotionSignalsResponse(BaseModel):
      signals      : list[PromotionSignal]
      generated_at : datetime
      policy_id    : str
      lookback_days : int

PipelineState additions:

  tier_policy_id      : str | None = None
  tier_policy_version : int | None = None

AuditRecord additions:

  tier_policy_id      : str | None = None
  tier_policy_version : int | None = None

Parity: ExceptionSignal, TierPolicy, TierPolicyUpdate, DrugClassBand,
PromotionSignal mirror into src/types.ts. wire-types-freshness CI job gates
on no drift.

================================================================================
7. API CHANGES
================================================================================

New endpoints
-------------

GET /api/admin/tier-policy
  Auth    : Any authenticated session or Bearer.
  Response: { policy: TierPolicy }

PATCH /api/admin/tier-policy
  Auth    : tenant_admin or platform_admin role only (403 otherwise).
  Body    : TierPolicyUpdate
  Response: { active_policy: TierPolicy, history_entry: TierBandHistoryEntry }
  422     : routine_floor < complex_floor + 0.01

GET /api/admin/tier-policy/history
  Auth    : tenant_admin or platform_admin role.
  Response: { history: TierBandHistoryEntry[] } (newest first)

GET /api/admin/tier-policy/promotion-signals
  Auth    : tenant_admin or platform_admin role.
  Response: PromotionSignalsResponse
  Params  : lookback_days (int, 1-365, default from PROMOTION_LOOKBACK_DAYS)

Modified: tier_router.py signature
------------------------------------

  decide_tier(signals: TierSignals, policy: TierPolicy) -> CaseTier

The TierSignals type is unchanged (existing callers pass signals exactly as
before). The second policy argument is new -- the node wrapper loads the policy
and passes it in; the pure function signature change is propagated through all
existing call sites (2: the node wrapper, the unit tests).

AuditRecord shape change
-------------------------

tier_policy_id and tier_policy_version added as nullable fields in
GET /api/audit/records response. Additive change; existing consumers ignore
new fields.

================================================================================
8. LANGGRAPH INTEGRATION
================================================================================

tier_router node wrapper update (agents/nodes/tier_router.py)
--------------------------------------------------------------

  async def run_tier_router(
      state: PipelineState, config: RunnableConfig
  ) -> PipelineState:
      """Wrapper node -- loads policy, delegates to pure decide_tier."""
      tenant_id = state["request"].tenant_id
      policy    = await PolicyStore.get_active(tenant_id)   # cached, async
      signals   = TierSignals.from_state(state)
      tier      = decide_tier(signals, policy)              # pure -- no I/O
      return {
          **state,
          "tier"               : tier,
          "workflow_plan"      : _extract_workflow_plan(state, tier),
          "tier_policy_id"     : policy.policy_id,
          "tier_policy_version": policy.version,
      }

Key invariants preserved:
  - decide_tier remains a pure function (no I/O, no DB call, no LLM call).
  - The node wrapper is the only I/O boundary.
  - The LangGraph wrapper pattern (thin async wrapper -> pure delegate) is
    unchanged.
  - No new conditional edges; no graph topology change.

Graph (agents/graph.py)
------------------------

_PIPELINE is unchanged in topology. run_tier_router now requires async (it was
already async due to LangGraph node semantics). The PolicyStore singleton is
initialized in the lifespan handler alongside the DB pool.

================================================================================
9. NEW MODULE: backend/db/policy_store.py
================================================================================

  backend/db/
  +-- policy_store.py   # PolicyStore: get_active, update, invalidate_cache,
                        #              history, promotion_signals

PolicyStore interface:

  class PolicyStore:
      _cache : dict[str | None, tuple[TierPolicy, datetime]]
      _ttl   : int = 60   # seconds

      async def get_active(
          self, tenant_id: str | None
      ) -> TierPolicy:
          """Cache-first; falls back to platform default on miss."""

      async def update(
          self, tenant_id: str | None,
          update: TierPolicyUpdate, changed_by: str
      ) -> tuple[TierPolicy, TierBandHistoryEntry]:
          """Atomic: deactivate old, insert new, write history row."""

      def invalidate_cache(self, tenant_id: str | None) -> None:
          """Called immediately after update() to force fresh load."""

      async def history(
          self, tenant_id: str | None
      ) -> list[TierBandHistoryEntry]: ...

      async def promotion_signals(
          self, tenant_id: str | None,
          lookback_days: int, threshold: int
      ) -> PromotionSignalsResponse: ...

Platform-default seeding (Alembic 0002_tier_policy.py upgrade function):

  op.execute("""
      INSERT INTO tier_policies (
          tenant_id, version, routine_floor, complex_floor,
          exception_signals, is_active, effective_from
      )
      VALUES (
          NULL, 1, 0.95, 0.70,
          '["generic_resolution","drug_alias_first_pairing","counter_offer",
            "novel_denial_reason","gatekeeper_exhausted"]',
          true, now()
      )
      ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
  """)

================================================================================
10. UI SURFACES
================================================================================

Backend slice only. The Build-view policy editor in the demo
(src/components/portfolio/BuildView.tsx) currently runs on fixture data. When
the live endpoints exist, the capability manifest (src/capabilities.ts, unit
B8) transitions it from simulated -> live. The live Build view calls:

  GET  /api/admin/tier-policy                   -- display active bands
  PATCH /api/admin/tier-policy                  -- submit a band update
  GET  /api/admin/tier-policy/history           -- show configuration changelog
  GET  /api/admin/tier-policy/promotion-signals -- show advisory signal table

The Sponsor view aggregation surface becomes the Scale view's tier performance
panel (capability unit S12, separate Workstream SU task).

No fixture-path changes are required for simulated mode -- the manifest seam
preserves the offline demo behavior.

================================================================================
11. TEST CASES
================================================================================

Unit (backend/tests/unit/)
---------------------------

Module: test_tier_router_node.py (extend)
  - decide_tier with custom routine_floor=0.98 routes a 0.96-confidence case
    to complex not routine
  - DrugClassBand override takes precedence over tenant-level floor
  - disabled ExceptionSignal does not escalate to exception
  - gatekeeper_exhausted always escalates regardless of bands

Module: test_policy_store.py
  - get_active returns platform default when no tenant override exists
  - cache hit does not issue a DB call
  - invalidate_cache forces fresh load on next call
  - update writes history row and deactivates old policy

Module: test_policy_validation.py
  - routine_floor < complex_floor + 0.01 raises ValidationError
  - drug_class override floor > parent tenant floor raises ValidationError
  - rationale required on update

Module: test_promotion_signal_aggregator.py
  - Drug/plan pairs below threshold excluded
  - suggested_complex_floor never exceeds routine_floor - 0.01
  - lookback window filter applied
  - empty audit store returns empty signals list

Module: test_tier_policy_audit_record.py
  - AuditRecord written post-S10 carries non-null tier_policy_id and
    tier_policy_version
  - pre-S10 records (nullable fields) do not break deserialization

Module: test_exception_signal_parity.py
  - ExceptionSignal enum in schemas.py and src/types.ts are identical

Contract
--------

test_schema_parity.py extended: ExceptionSignal, TierPolicy present in both
sides.
wire-types-freshness CI job: TierPolicyUpdate, PromotionSignal,
TierBandHistoryEntry in generated types.

Integration (backend/tests/integration/)
-----------------------------------------

Module: test_tier_policy_endpoints.py
  - GET returns platform default for Bearer
  - PATCH with tenant_admin role creates new version
  - PATCH with operate role returns 403
  - invalid floors return 422
  - history endpoint returns newest-first
  - promotion-signals endpoint returns correct counts
  - promotion-signals threshold filter works

Module: test_tier_router_with_policy.py
  - Full pipeline run writes tier_policy_id on AuditRecord
  - PATCH to new floor + next pipeline run uses new floor
  - cache invalidation tested via TTL mock

Module: test_policy_change_audit.py
  - PATCH creates an AuditRecord with lifecycle=policy_change
  - policy-change record visible in GET /api/audit/records for platform-admin
  - tenant-scoped session sees only own policy changes

Regulatory compliance test
---------------------------

test_statutory_floor.py (tagged: regulatory)
  - Platform-default policy has routine_floor=0.95 (Illinois HB statutory
    floor).
  - No PATCH to the platform-default policy (tenant_id=NULL) can set
    routine_floor < 0.95 (enforced by a platform_admin-only validation layer
    distinct from the general floor validation).

================================================================================
12. RISKS
================================================================================

Risk: Policy cache stale window allows routing under a revoked policy
  Likelihood: Low | Impact: Medium
  Mitigation: TTL is 60 s (configurable); invalidate_cache() is called
  synchronously at update time on the same worker; multi-worker setups need a
  shared cache (Redis) -- deferred note in ADR.

Risk: decide_tier signature change breaks existing unit tests
  Likelihood: Medium | Impact: Low
  Mitigation: All 2 call sites updated in the same PR; TDD RED test written
  first; no other importer.

Risk: Drug-class matching ambiguity (one drug in two classes)
  Likelihood: Low | Impact: Medium
  Mitigation: DrugClassBand uses exact string match on drug_class; first-match
  wins; admin documentation required.

Risk: Promotion-signal aggregation query too slow on large audit_records table
  Likelihood: Low | Impact: High
  Mitigation: Query bounded by lookback_days (default 90) and filtered by
  tenant_id; index on (tenant_id, created_at, tier, provenance) added in
  migration.

Risk: platform_admin bypasses routine_floor >= 0.95 statutory guard
  Likelihood: Low | Impact: Critical
  Mitigation: Statutory floor validation is a separate hard-coded check (not
  policy-configurable); tested in test_statutory_floor.py (regulatory tag).

Risk: TierBandHistory diff_summary leaks PHI via field values
  Likelihood: Low | Impact: High
  Mitigation: diff_summary records only numeric floor values and signal names
  -- no drug/patient text; validated by PHI scan in test_golden_compliance.py.
